narration_timeline.text: Why does this mantis hold its front legs up, almost like it is waving?
narration_timeline.scene: Real mantis shown raising its forelegs in threat display.

narration_timeline.text: Those folded legs have spines that help the insect grip things close to its body.
narration_timeline.scene: Close image of folded forelegs on a live mantis.

narration_timeline.text: When a smaller insect is caught, the mantis uses those arms to keep its meal from escaping.
narration_timeline.scene: Mantis interacting with real insect prey in two separate recordings.

narration_timeline.text: Other close recordings show how carefully the animal positions those same front legs.
narration_timeline.scene: Authentic close-up of a mantis moving or holding its forelegs.

narration_timeline.text: A raised posture can also appear when a mantis responds to something around it.
narration_timeline.scene: Mantis posture in a separate outdoor New York recording.

narration_timeline.text: Whether it is handling prey or holding still, those front legs are its most remarkable tools.
narration_timeline.scene: Two separate mantis close-ups of foreleg posture.
